text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are concerned about your infant's bilious vomiting and inability to pass meconium. How old is the baby, and was the delivery vaginal or by cesarean section?

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to perform a physical examination of the infant's abdomen and rectum to assess for signs of obstruction or a mass. I will also check for any visible abdominal wall defects or unusual skin pigmentation.

text: I will now examine the infant's abdomen for any masses and perform a digital rectal exam to check for a tight sphincter or empty rectum. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings confirm a distal obstruction. I will now perform a digital rectal exam to check for a tight sphincter or empty rectum, which would support Hirschsprung's disease. REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Enema

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal contrast enema makes Hirschsprung's disease less likely, so I need to consider other causes of distal obstruction. Does the infant have a history of maternal diabetes, and has there been any evidence of a meconium plug or sludge on prior imaging?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Newborn, no prior medical history. Birth was uneventful. Social history: The infant is the first child of the family. No known family history of genetic or congenital diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and failure to pass meconium with a normal contrast enema, I suspect a distal intestinal obstruction such as meconium ileus or ileal atresia. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ultrasound makes meconium ileus less likely, pointing toward a mechanical obstruction like jejunal or ileal atresia. I will request a CT scan to visualize the bowel structure and confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rectal biopsy results are definitive, showing an absence of ganglion cells. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease
